name: Warm-up and cool-down protocol
keyTakeaways: Warm up every time, in three parts: about 5–10 minutes of easy cardio, then a few minutes of dynamic (moving) drills, then lighter "ramp-up" sets of your first weighted exercise. Warm-ups improved performance in most of the outcomes measured in a 2010 meta-analysis and rarely made anything worse.
Easy means easy: you should be able to talk in full sentences and maybe break a light sweat. If you finish the warm-up tired, it was too hard.

Before lifting, choose moving stretches over long holds. Short static holds (30 seconds or less per muscle) inside a full warm-up have only a tiny effect on strength. Holds of 60 seconds or more per muscle cause a clearer strength loss, so save long holds for after the session.
Ramp-up sets do the job of a "specific warm-up" for each big lift: 2–4 lighter sets that get heavier, with fewer reps as you go, and none of them close to failure.

A cool-down lets your heart rate come down gradually and helps you feel steady. Don't expect it to stop next-day soreness. Reviews find that stretching after exercise does little or nothing for muscle soreness (DOMS). The cool-down is still the best time for flexibility work, because your muscles are warm.
appGuidance: Every gym session starts with an automatic Warm-up block of three stages: (1) General cardio, 5 min by default (user can set 5–10), at "easy, can talk"; (2) Dynamic drills, 3–5 picked automatically from the session's muscle focus (table 2.3); (3) Ramp-up sets inserted before the first exercise for each major movement.

Ramp-up sets are calculated from the planned working weight and rep range using table 2.4, rounded down to the nearest available plate or stack step. Label them "Warm-up set" and exclude them from volume and progress statistics.
On machines and for exercises after the first one for the same muscle, offer just one optional "feeler" set at about 50% × 10.
Every session ends with a Cool-down block: 3–5 min of easy cardio, then 3–4 static stretches for the muscles trained, with a 30 s hold timer, 2 rounds by default.
Time-crunch mode: warm-up shrinks to 3 min of cardio, 2 drills and 1–2 ramp sets; cool-down shrinks to 3 min (est.). Never remove ramp sets before a heavy barbell lift.
Users aged 65 or over: default hold time 30–60 s.
Warm-up start: "Easy pace. You should be able to chat. A light sweat is perfect."
Dynamic drills: "Move smoothly through a comfortable range. No bouncing."
Ramp-up set: "Light set to practise your form. Stop well before it gets hard."
Before working sets: "Warm-up done. Your first working set starts now."
Cool-down: "Slow down gradually. Keep moving until your breathing settles."
Stretch: "Ease in until you feel a gentle stretch, not pain. Breathe slowly and hold."
Soreness tip (FAQ): "Some soreness 1–3 days after a new workout is normal. Stretching won't prevent it, but building up gradually helps."
Safety: "Feel dizzy, chest pain or unusually breathless? Stop, sit or lie down, and get medical help if it doesn't pass quickly."
Do not schedule static-stretch holds of 60 s or more per muscle before strength blocks.
If the session has no weighted exercises (bodyweight or cardio), skip ramp sets; the general warm-up builds gradually instead.
For the Gym 50 beginner plan: warm-up about 12 min plus cool-down about 7 min (est.) should fit inside the session time shown to the user.

rules.then: insert a general warm-up of 5 min (user range 5-10 min) of easy cardio on treadmill, bike, elliptical or rower at a conversational pace (RPE about 3-4/10, est.)
rules.source: ACSM (via secondary sources); Mayo Clinic; NHS

rules.if: session is heavy (main lifts at RPE 8 or above) or user is new or the gym is cold
rules.then: extend the general warm-up toward 10 min
add 3-6 dynamic drills matched to the session's muscle focus, 8-10 reps or 20-30 s each, about 3-5 min total
rules.source: ACE; Jeffreys RAMP model (NSCA/UKSCA); Opplert & Babault 2018

rules.if: a static stretch is placed before strength exercises
rules.then: limit it to 30 s or less per hold and per muscle, and never schedule holds of 60 s or more per muscle before lifting
rules.source: Behm et al. 2016; Chaabene et al. 2019; Warneke & Lohmann 2024

rules.if: first exercise for a major movement with working sets of 3-6 reps (heavy)
rules.then: insert ramp-up sets: empty bar or 40% x 8, 60% x 5, 75-80% x 3, optional 85-90% x 1-2 of working weight, 1-2 min rest (est.)
rules.source: Ribeiro et al. 2020; NSCA 1RM test warm-up (via HPRC); FitPlate synthesis (est.)

rules.if: first exercise for a major movement with working sets of 8-12 reps (moderate)
rules.then: insert ramp-up sets: 40% x 8-10, then 60-70% x 5-6 of working weight, about 60 s rest (est.)
rules.source: Ribeiro et al. 2020; NSCA 1RM test warm-up (via HPRC); FitPlate synthesis (est.)

rules.if: machine exercise or a later exercise for an already-warmed muscle
rules.then: offer one optional feeler set at about 50% of working weight x 10-12 (est.)

rules.if: a set is labelled warm-up or ramp-up
rules.then: keep it at 4 or more reps in reserve (est.) and exclude it from volume and progress statistics
insert 3-5 min of easy cardio (slow walk or easy spin) before the user stops
rules.source: Mayo Clinic; NHS / Live Well South West

rules.then: add 3-4 static stretches for muscles trained, each held 10-30 s at mild tension without bouncing, about 60 s total per muscle
rules.source: ACSM flexibility guidelines; Mayo Clinic; Harvard Health (via secondary sources)

rules.then: set default static hold time to 30-60 s
rules.source: ACSM stretching and flexibility guidelines update (2021)

rules.if: app text describes the purpose of stretching or the cool-down
rules.then: never claim it prevents muscle soreness (DOMS) or injury; describe it as flexibility work and a gradual return to rest
rules.source: Herbert et al. Cochrane review 2011; Afonso et al. 2021

rules.then: shorten the warm-up to 3 min cardio, 2 drills and 1-2 ramp sets, and the cool-down to 3 min easy cardio (est.); never drop ramp sets before a heavy barbell lift

rules.if: user reports dizziness, chest pain or unusual breathlessness during the warm-up or cool-down
rules.then: stop the session, advise sitting or lying down, and show the seek-medical-help message
